taxonomy.subtopic: Different decussation levels of corticospinal, dorsal-column, and spinothalamic pathways

questions.stem_html: A man sustains a penetrating injury to the left half of the spinal cord at T9. One week later, examination below the lesion shows left-sided spastic weakness and loss of vibration sense, with right-sided loss of pain and temperature beginning several segments below T9. The accompanying cord diagram traces the affected pathways. Which anatomic arrangement best explains this combination?

options.text_html: Corticospinal and dorsal-column pathways cross in the caudal medulla, whereas spinothalamic fibers cross near their spinal entry level
All three pathways cross in the caudal medulla before ascending or descending in the spinal cord
Corticospinal fibers cross segmentally in the anterior white commissure, whereas pain fibers remain ipsilateral to the thalamus
Dorsal-column fibers cross immediately on entering the cord, while corticospinal and spinothalamic fibers remain uncrossed
Spinothalamic fibers descend ipsilaterally to the sacral cord before crossing and ascending

questions.explanation_html: Lateral corticospinal fibers cross at the pyramidal decussation in the caudal medulla and then descend ipsilaterally in the spinal cord. Dorsal-column fibers also ascend ipsilaterally and cross in the medulla. In contrast, pain and temperature fibers synapse shortly after entering the cord and second-order axons cross through the anterior white commissure, usually within one to two segments. A left hemicord lesion therefore causes ipsilateral motor and vibration/proprioception loss with contralateral pain-temperature loss beginning slightly below the lesion.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Spinothalamic fibers cross in the spinal cord, not in the medulla.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: The corticospinal tract crosses in the caudal medulla, and spinothalamic second-order fibers cross segmentally in the cord.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Dorsal-column fibers remain ipsilateral in the cord and cross only after synapsing in the medulla.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Pain-temperature fibers may ascend or descend a short distance in Lissauer tract, but they do not travel to the sacral cord before crossing.

questions.educational_objective: A spinal hemisection causes ipsilateral corticospinal and dorsal-column deficits but contralateral pain-temperature loss because spinothalamic fibers cross near their level of entry.
